topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement system and frames its conceptual importance and complexity within immunology.

topics.label: Overview, nomenclature, and central role of complement component C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the foundational architecture of the complement cascade, its naming conventions, and the central role of C3 as the fulcrum of activation.

topics.label: Pathways and threshold of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct recognition pathways that drive C3 convertase formation and establish the threshold for complement activation.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream processes through which activated complement destroys pathogens and drives inflammation.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the specialized regulatory proteins that prevent complement from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the distinct clinical presentations and disease patterns associated with deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion strategies against complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how microbial pathogens counteract complement-mediated clearance, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the discussion of complement and provides a brief preview of the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
